title.raw: Dense fog could reduce visibility to half a mile overnight and early Wednesday morning
title.rendered: Dense fog could reduce visibility to half a mile overnight and early Wednesday morning

excerpt.raw: Patchy dense fog is expected to reduce visibility across the Highway 84 corridor late tonight and early Wednesday morning, prompting caution for drivers.
excerpt.rendered: Patchy dense fog is expected to reduce visibility across the Highway 84 corridor late tonight and early Wednesday morning, prompting caution for drivers.

content.raw:
Patchy dense fog is expected to develop late tonight across the Highway 84 corridor, reducing visibility to half a mile or less, according to the National Weather Service.

The fog is forecast to persist between 5 a.m. and 9 a.m. Wednesday, affecting morning commuters. Drivers are urged to slow down and use low beam headlights in areas of dense fog to improve safety.

Officials advise motorists to exercise caution and allow extra time for travel during this period. No other weather warnings have been issued at this time.

Source: Original Article

payload.title: NWS forecast called for dense fog Tuesday morning, Oct. 13
payload.excerpt: The National Weather Service forecast patchy dense fog along the Highway 84 corridor from 5 to 9 a.m. Tuesday, Oct. 13.
payload.content:
The National Weather Service forecast patchy dense fog along the Highway 84 corridor between 5 and 9 a.m. Tuesday, Oct. 13, with visibility potentially falling to half a mile or less.

The agency urged drivers encountering fog to slow down, use low-beam headlights and allow extra travel time.

Correction (Oct. 13, 2026): The forecast applied to Tuesday morning, not Wednesday morning.

Source: National Weather Service Jackson

title.raw: Greenville, Mississippi, claims state’s only top 10 ranking
title.rendered: Greenville, Mississippi, claims state’s only top 10 ranking

excerpt.raw: Greenville is the only city in Mississippi to make the top ten list, according to local officials and tourism authorities.
excerpt.rendered: Greenville is the only city in Mississippi to make the top ten list, according to local officials and tourism authorities.

content.raw:
Greenville, Mississippi, is the only city in the state to rank in the top ten, according to local sources. The city’s recognition highlights its significance within Mississippi’s tourism and economic landscape.

The Mississippi Development Authority, Visit Mississippi, the Greenville-Washington County Convention & Visitors Bureau, Entergy Mississippi, and the city government all acknowledge Greenville's distinction. They emphasize the city’s role as a key destination in the state.

Officials say the ranking brings attention to Greenville’s attractions and economic vitality. They also note ongoing efforts to promote tourism and community development in the region.

Source: Original Article

payload.title: Doe’s Eat Place in Greenville ranks eighth on Discovery Matt’s Southern restaurant list
payload.excerpt: A Discovery Matt editorial list places Doe’s Eat Place in Greenville eighth among 35 old-school Southern restaurants.
payload.content:
Doe’s Eat Place in Greenville is ranked eighth on Discovery Matt’s editorial list of 35 old-school restaurants in the South.

Delta Compass – WCEA shared the list on Facebook, highlighting Greenville’s entry. The graphic lists Doe’s Eat Place as the only Mississippi restaurant in its top 10.

Correction (Oct. 13, 2026): The list ranks restaurants, not cities. An earlier version also attributed comments to agencies without supporting statements.

Source: Delta Compass – WCEA announcement and ranking graphic

title.raw: Mississippi Delta Community College to host coronation during 100th Homecoming
title.rendered: Mississippi Delta Community College to host coronation during 100th Homecoming

excerpt.raw: The college will celebrate its 100th anniversary with a coronation event for student leaders on October 13, 2026.
excerpt.rendered: The college will celebrate its 100th anniversary with a coronation event for student leaders on October 13, 2026.

content.raw:
Mississippi Delta Community College will host a coronation event during its 100th anniversary Homecoming celebration on Oct. 13, 2026. The event will recognize the college’s Mister and Miss Mississippi Delta Community College, highlighting student leadership.

The coronation is scheduled for 7 p.m. at J.T. Hall Coliseum. Organizers encourage attendees to dress formal and participate in the evening of tradition and celebration, according to a college spokesperson.

MDCC officials said the event is part of the college’s centennial festivities, which aim to honor its history of academic excellence and community involvement. The college’s 100th anniversary marks a century of educational service in the region.

For more information, attendees are encouraged to follow MDCC’s official social media channels using the hashtags #MDCC, #MSDelta, and #ForwardTogether.

Source: Original Article

content.raw:
Mississippi Delta Community College is hosting a black-tie coronation event as part of its 100th anniversary homecoming celebration. The evening will honor Mister and Miss Mississippi Delta Community College and recognize student leaders.

The event is scheduled for Tuesday, October 13, 2026, at 7 p.m. at J.T. Hall Coliseum, according to college officials. Attendees are encouraged to dress formally for the occasion, which promises an evening of elegance and tradition.

College representatives said the event continues the institution’s celebration of a century of academic excellence and community impact. The event is also part of the college’s ongoing efforts to honor its history and future, officials added.

Participants and guests are invited to join the festivities and be part of this milestone moment for the college, which has a longstanding legacy in the region.

Source: Original Article
